citations.text: Hanisch, S., & Eirdosh, D. (2023). Behavioral science and education for sustainable development: Towards metacognitive competency. Sustainability, 15(9), 7413.

en.general: A capacity to use concepts about human behaviour, including one's own thoughts and feelings counted as behaviour, to understand why people act as they do and to keep or change one's own behaviour in line with chosen values. The design concept names its two parts conceptual understanding of human behaviour and adaptive flexibility.

examples: A student maps why a classmate withdraws from group work, notices that her own irritation is part of the pattern, and picks a response that fits what she values.
A teacher uses a payoff matrix from one lesson to explain a different situation and says where the comparison fails.
nonExamples: Memorising a list of behavioural-science terms.
Following a rule about the right way to behave without any understanding of why.
